advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the cutover surface is intentionally landed unwired (incremental), or wire route_for/coordinate_and_fuse into the live dispatch path.
evidence: search for coordinate_and_fuse: only batch_dispatch.py definition + tests reference it
search for the reconciler route_for: only batch_dispatch.py definition + tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/mutate/test_operation_coordinator.py reference it

advisory.finding: The commit title claims 'Cut over non-create routing to coordinator+fuse', but route_for / coordinate_and_fuse / build_pass_tally have no production caller — applier / apply_handlers / apply_outbound do not invoke them; only tests reference the new functions.
scenarios: A reviewer or operator assumes non-create mutations now flow through the coordinator+fuse based on the commit message, but the legacy per-mutation dispatch path is still the only one executed at runtime.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a build_pass_tally test with a nonzero recovered bucket (a plan whose execute returns status='recovered') asserting applied_count == applied + recovered and recovered_count > 0.
evidence: docstring at batch_dispatch.py:329-331 declares 'applied_count folds recovered into applied'
test_operation_coordinator.py:988 `assert tally["recovered_count"] == 0` (the only build_pass_tally happy-path test)

ABSENCE: no test feeds a plan whose execute returns status='recovered' into coordinate_and_fuse then asserts applied_count includes that recovered outcome; coordinator DOES produce a 'recovered' bucket (test_recovered_op_is_recovered_bucket at test_operation_coordinator.py:595)
advisory.finding: build_pass_tally's recovered-into-applied fold (`applied_count = tallies['applied'] + tallies['recovered']`) is never exercised with a nonzero recovered bucket; both build_pass_tally tests assert recovered_count == 0, so a regression dropping the `+ tallies['recovered']` term would leave all tests green.
scenarios: A refactor drops or mistypes the `+ tallies['recovered']` term; recovered mutations silently stop counting toward applied_count and no test fails.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a case: a plan whose scripted execute returns AtomicSignal(status='recovered') alongside an applied plan, then assert build_pass_tally(report)['applied_count'] == 2 and ['recovered_count'] == 1.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide whether _fuse_one should preserve a genuine hard-failure bucket (permanent_failure/exhausted_transient) rather than reclassify every non-success under an open scope to 'deferred'.
evidence: batch_dispatch.py:261 `if decision is not None and not policy.is_success(outcome.disposition):` then returns bucket="deferred" for any non-success disposition
failure_policy maps permanent_failure/exhausted_transient to bucket 'failed' (failure_policy.py:64-65), but a matching-scope reclassification overwrites that with 'deferred'
reconcile.py:734 `mutation_failures = int(apply_tally.get("failed_count", 0))` — a ticket masked to deferred no longer contributes to failed_count
tests only exercise this with a transient-exhaustion ticket (test_operation_coordinator.py:894-897 T-4), never a permanent_failure under an open scope
blocking.finding: _fuse_one reclassifies EVERY non-success coordinator outcome under an already-open scope to the 'deferred' bucket, discarding its original bucket — so a genuine permanent_failure (or exhausted_transient) on a later matching ticket is masked as a deferral and drops out of failed_count / the degraded exit.
scenarios: An endpoint fuse opens after three budget-exhaustions, then a fourth ticket on that endpoint fails with a genuine permanent_failure (e.g. 403) — it is reported as deferred, not failed.
